newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia court sells off bankrupt Urals gold mine.
newsitem.headline: Russia court sells off bankrupt Urals gold mine.

text.p: A Russian civil court ordered the assets of a big gold mine in the Sverdlovsk region near Yekaterinburg in the Urals to be sold off, Interfax news agency said on Monday.

Interfax quoted local administration sources as saying Uralelektromed copper plant was planning to buy assets of the Berezovsky mine. A private investor had already bought part of the Berezovsky gold mine worth 2.4 billion roubles, it said.

The agency said the local prosecutor's office wanted Mikrodin, which owns 78 percent of the gold mine, to repay a $3.5 million credit the government had granted for the mine's development, plus interest.
Mikrodin is part of the Interros finance industrial group, which is closely associated with Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian).

The court initiated bankruptcy proceedings against the mine in September. Berezovsky gold mine used to produce about two tonnes of gold a year, but output has slumped to a mere 30 kg a month in 1996. --Andrei Khalip, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
